## 3. Build modes

The build script runs in one of four modes:

| mode | when | C |
|---|---|---|
| bundled | by default, but for a wrapper whose `c/` is still its whole library | `c/`, built statically into `OUT_DIR` by the target's own build system, in the configuration of the `plain` variant |
| shared | the `shared` feature | `c/`, built as shared libraries into `OUT_DIR`, the same way |
| system | the `system` feature, and by default for a wrapper whose `c/` is still its whole library | an install, found through `<LIB>_DIR`, then `pkg-config` |
| campaign | `CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT` names a variant, or `CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR` a private build | the variant's build, recorded in `crustify/artifacts/build.json`: its static archive, when it records one, else its shared libraries |

The campaign's repository sets `CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT` to `plain` in its
`.cargo/config.toml`, so that every build there runs in campaign mode unless the variable
names another variant, or is set empty to build as a dependent would.

In every mode, `shims.c` and `static_fns.c` are compiled against the headers the bindings
match, with the instrumentation of the C they link, and the bindings are the committed
ones unless the `bindgen` feature regenerates them into `OUT_DIR` from the headers of that
C. Campaign mode's tests and gates always regenerate them.

Bundled mode links the C statically, so that the bindings and the C they call always come
from the same revision; it sets no rpath. It builds `c/` against the out-of-tree libraries
its configuration uses as the target's build system finds them on the building host; a
dependent whose host lacks one supplies it through that build system's own search paths,
such as `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` and `PKG_CONFIG_PATH`. Shared mode leaves the remaining C's references
to ported modules undefined in its shared libraries, and the build script has the final
binary export what resolves them (`-Wl,--export-dynamic-symbol=<name>` for each export),
as a cdylib already does; the libraries are found beside the binary, through an `$ORIGIN`
rpath, and ship with it.

System mode serves a crate whose `c/` is still the whole source: once a port campaign has
switched a module, an install of the library would hold that module's C beside the Rust
that replaces it, and the build fails, naming the switched modules. It checks the
version: the library found must be the one the bindings were generated from, as its build
system reports it (`pkg-config --modversion`), or, for an out-of-tree library's wrapper, a
release ABI-compatible with it, which shares its soname. Another version fails the build
with both versions named, unless the `bindgen` feature regenerates the bindings for it. Each link
unit's module exports the version the bindings match as `C_VERSION`. `<LIB>_DIR` names an
install prefix: the build reads the headers under its `include/`, links the library under
its `lib/`, and takes the version from `lib/pkgconfig/<lib>.pc`. Without it, `pkg-config`
finds the library, which is linked as `pkg-config` resolves it, with no rpath.

An install carries neither the internal headers nor the functions its shared library does
not export, whichever header declares them, public or internal, and the shared libraries
shared mode builds lack the same functions, since the target's own configuration builds
them. Once the bindings reach either, system mode cannot serve the crate, nor shared mode
once they reach a function a shared library hides: the build fails in each, naming what
the library lacks, as system mode fails for a switched module, and bundled mode, whose
build in `OUT_DIR` has both, becomes the crate's default. The `bindgen` feature then regenerates from that build's
headers, never from an install's.

A link unit the target links as an executable, such as a command-line tool, has no
library. Bundled mode compiles its translation units as the target's build system records
them, without linking the executable, archives their objects and links the archive;
campaign mode links them from the variant's static archive, which holds them, as
[`setup`](../../workflows/setup/SKILL.md)'s Builds section describes; shared and system
modes, which link libraries, refuse its feature, naming the modes that serve it. An archive
member is linked only where one of its symbols is referenced, so a test that references
the translation unit defining the executable's `main`, directly or through another member
that references it, links a second `main` beside its harness's and fails to link. That
unit's other symbols are therefore ported to exports first, so that the members which
reference them stop pulling it in, and until then the units that pull it in are tested
through the variant's executable, run as a child process.

Campaign mode serves the campaign while it extends the bindings: batches add allowlist
entries and shims, and the bindings follow from them. It needs bindgen, which the safe
crate enables for its own tests through a dev-dependency on itself with the `bindgen`
feature, so that the campaign's tests and gates regenerate while dependents build from
the committed bindings. A build that does not enable the feature, such as the crate's
documentation, uses the committed bindings unchecked; the tests and gates always enable it.
The bindings it generates are compared with the committed ones: a difference fails the
build, naming the regenerated file, unless `CRUSTIFY_BINDINGS_UPDATE` is set, in which case
they are written over `bindings.rs` and `static_fns.c`. It links the C the variant built,
so that every test runs against the instrumented C it was built for. A variant that
records a `static` archive, as [`setup`](../../workflows/setup/SKILL.md)'s Builds section
describes, has it linked statically, with the libraries its shared library links, so that
the Rust reaches the internal functions the shared library does not export, and the
remaining C resolves the exports within the same link, as bundled mode's does; only the
out-of-tree libraries' installs of the same variant take an rpath. A variant that records
none has its shared libraries linked with an rpath to them, and the test binaries export
what the remaining C resolves to, as shared mode does.

No build links two copies of a module: a mode links either a module's C or the Rust that
replaces it, never both, and the Rust static library that the target's remaining C links
from a module's switch on carries no C of its own, as the porting workflow's Builds
section describes.

## 4. Extending

The bindings grow with the batches: a batch whose items need a raw binding the bindings
lack extends its own link unit's input, and nothing else:

1. its link unit's `allowlist.txt` gains only the FFI items its items need, and
   `wrapper.h` an internal header only when one of them is declared there;
2. a shim is added to `shims.h` and `shims.c` only for a macro whose expansion depends on
   the build's configuration, as `crustify_<NAME>`, as
   [`binding-symbols`](../binding/symbols/SKILL.md)'s Macros section describes;
3. the bindings are regenerated, in campaign mode with `CRUSTIFY_BINDINGS_UPDATE` set; and
4. the safe crate is built and tested against them.

Where its link unit's headers name a type another link unit owns, the batch also extends
what the re-export needs, and only that: the type joins its own link unit's `external.txt`,
the owning link unit's `allowlist.txt` too while its bindings lack the type, and the link
unit's module in `src/sys.rs` re-exports it from the owner's, under its C name.

An allowlist or `wrapper.h` change alone leaves the C library as it is, so it reuses a
prebuilt variant; a shim compiles with the crate, as [Build modes](#3-build-modes) describes.

## 5. Landing

A batch that changes an allowlist, `external.txt`, a shim or `wrapper.h` regenerates the
bindings and commits them in the same landing, so that the committed bindings always match
their input. The gates that check it, and that the crate packages, are
[`testing-gates`](../../verification/testing/gates/SKILL.md)'s Regressions section's.

## 6. Publishing

The safe crate is published with its raw bindings and the C it bundles. The packaged crate
holds the layout above, `src/`, the files of `c/` that the bundled build reads and the
C's license files, and nothing else of the repository but its README and the files the
package manager adds to every package, such as its manifest's original and its lockfile.

---
name: ffibox
description: "The library the campaign's Rust holds C memory through, in both directions: owners, handles, lifecycle policies, status conventions, callbacks and exports. Read before writing any wrapper, owner, lifecycle strategy, callable type or export, when judging a crate for adoption, and when testing or reviewing one."
---

# ffibox

ffibox is the library a campaign's Rust expresses C's ownership and lifetime conventions
through, in both directions: memory C allocates, frees, copies, refcounts or locks, held
from Rust behind a safe API, and memory Rust owns that C holds, calls or reads. Its
primitives stand in for raw pointers and hand-written `Drop` impls wherever C aliases a
value; what C does not alias is plain Rust.

Its `README.md` is read in full before the first wrapper is written, and each section
below names the documents under its `docs/` that its stage reads, also in full. Which
primitive serves which C declaration, and how each is built, is those documents'. A
representation ffibox cannot express is hand-written, as its `docs/hand-written.md`
describes, with the same seam and safety-comment discipline. Its goals and non-goals,
`docs/goals.md`, are what a change to ffibox is judged against, as
[`evolution`](../../crustify/evolution/SKILL.md) describes.

What follows is how ffibox serves each stage: each section names the skill and section it
adds to, and states only what ffibox adds there.

## Planning
## Binding and porting

Binding reads `docs/ownership.md`, `docs/borrows.md`, `docs/patterns.md`,
`docs/vtables.md` and `docs/hand-written.md`; porting reads `docs/outbound.md` too.

### Binding types

A type that stays interoperable with C is bound through ffibox's primitives wherever they
apply, as `docs/ownership.md` and `docs/borrows.md` walk from its C declaration to them.

### Binding types › Safe layout

While a type keeps its C layout, `define_ctype!` mints `Foo`, `FooRef<'a>` and `FooMut<'a>`,
and its owners are aliases of ffibox's owners over the policy that names its lifecycle
routines: `pub type FooBox = CBox<Foo, FooFree>;`, and `CArc<Foo, P>` for `FooArc`. A
value held inline that disposes its resources on drop is a `CVal<Foo, P>`.

### Binding symbols › Functions

A C routine's status convention becomes a `Result` through `status`, an object returned
through an out-parameter a return value through `from_c_out` or `from_raw_out`, and C's
iteration conventions iterators, as `docs/patterns.md` maps them.

### Binding symbols › Function pointers
### Porting › FFI boundary

An export gateway is built from the primitives `docs/outbound.md` chooses for what C does
with the Rust it reaches:

- the lifecycle routines C still calls on a ported type are `export_cnew!`,
  `export_cdrop!` and `export_cdupclone!` over the type's policy, which take and return
  its owners and handles;
- memory C frees comes from the allocator C frees it with: Rust's, `RustAlloc`, when C
  frees it through an exported release;
- a callback C passes an export is a `CFn` or a `CFnBox`, and a value C keeps a
  `CPayload`; and
- the gateway's body runs in `callback::barrier`.

### Porting types › Structs
## Testing

### Testing › UB tests

The public seam interface ffibox exports on a type is meant to be exercised inside the
crate only, as an escape hatch for external consumers, so it gets no UB tests: a test of
it, for UB or functionality, is a unit test.

## Reviewing
---
name: ffimap
description: "Deterministic counts and sites of a Rust crate's unsafe and FFI surface. Read before a batch lands (its safe-boundary scan and safety-audit cells), before planning an audit's worksets, and when reviewing for unsafety, contracts or UB."
---

# ffimap

ffimap maps a Rust crate's FFI and unsafe surface deterministically: a rustc driver over
HIR and typeck counts unsafe blocks and fns, raw and void pointers by position and
visibility, FFI calls and wrapper use. No model is involved, so two runs over one tree
agree exactly. Its `--help` lists its flags, and its `docs/schema.md`, read in full before
its first scan, its counters and how a report combines them.

It counts what the build compiles of the safe crate itself, and prints one JSON document:

```bash
ffimap <workdir> > <file>.json
```

Every scan names the crate's seams, the functions that hand a value between its wrapper and
its raw form, so that each counter's `of_which.seam` share tells that plumbing apart from
the pointer management a consumer of the safe API faces: ffibox's handle seams `as_ptr`,
`as_mut_ptr`, `as_void_ptr`, `from_ptr` and `from_void_ptr`, the ownership hand-offs
`from_raw_parts`, `into_raw_parts`, `into_raw`, `from_c`, `into_c` and `as_c_ptr`, the adoption of a raw C
value, `from_raw`, and the view of a C object as another, `as_object`. A crate built on
ffibox is scanned with `--ffibox`, and its `-sys` crates are named with `--sys-crates`:

```bash
ffimap <workdir> --ffibox --sys-crates <the -sys crates> --regions ffi_import,ffi_export \
    --seams as_ptr,as_mut_ptr,as_void_ptr,from_ptr,from_void_ptr,from_raw_parts,into_raw_parts,into_raw,from_c,into_c,as_c_ptr,from_raw,as_object \
## Binding and porting

### Binding › Safe boundary

Before a batch lands, a scan with `--sites fn.unsafe.pub raw_ptr.field.pub
raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.safe.pub raw_ptr.fn_sig_ret.safe.pub` lists the public
`unsafe fn`s and the raw pointers on the safe public interface, and each of those sites
that belongs to the batch's changeset and that a safe variant could replace is fixed.
Its `--sites` also name the unsafe code outside both regions,
`code.unsafe_block.of_which.outside_regions`, another crate's macro expansions included,
which the `unsafe_code` lint misses, and `fn.unsafe.of_which.outside_regions.pub` and
`.priv`: outside the raw bindings, each of those sites in the batch's changeset is moved
into its region.

## Accounting

### Accounting › Landing cells

A batch's row in the dashboard's `Batches: safety audit` table is the change in each of
the Safety audit's metrics, from a scan of the tip its landing rebased onto to a scan of
the tree it lands.

### Accounting › API stability

`ffimap api` measures a safe crate's consumer-facing API per C item, from rustdoc JSON, as
its `docs/api.md` describes, read in full before its first use. A C item is the
`<kind>::<path>` of a `Wraps` or `Replaces` anchor, its surface every stand-in the anchor
names and the handles and owners tied to it, each judged by the contract
[`binding-types`](../../rust/binding/types/SKILL.md)' Safe layout section gives a consumer:
the methods every form offers, its reborrows and dereferences, and the traits a consumer
can use, never a form's raw access or seams. A batch generates the safe crate's rustdoc
JSON on the tip its landing rebased onto and on the tree it lands, with a nightly whose
`format_version` the tool supports, and ffibox's, with private items, for the contracts of
the forms it defines:

```bash
cargo +<nightly> rustdoc -p <crate> --lib -- -Z unstable-options --output-format json
ffimap api diff <base>.json <tree>.json --dep <ffibox>.json --items "<the worklist's keys>" --format json
```

Each item comes out `kept`, `extended`, `changed`, `removed` or `new`, with its anchor's
move from `Wraps` to `Replaces` where a port made it. The batch's row in the dashboard's
`Batches: API stability` table counts them over its worklist, and over the crate's
unattributed public items, compared per module.

### Accounting › Records

An unseeded scan of the unsafe and FFI surface is recorded at each batch's, wave's and
the campaign's end, as `ffimap.json` in its artifact directory: a batch's in the run dir
of the run that landed it, a wave's in its wave's dir, as `layout` spells it, and the
campaign's in `crustify/artifacts/`. A module's end is the scan of the last wave of its `wrap` and `port` items.

## Reviewing

---
name: accounting
description: "The dashboard, its cells, the runs' records and transcripts, and how cost and time are derived. Read before filling dashboard cells or collecting a run's records."
---

# Accounting

What a campaign records about its own work: the dashboard, the runs' records and
transcripts its figures come from, and how cost and time are derived from them.

## 1. The dashboard

The dashboard, `crustify/artifacts/dashboard.md` unless the settings name another, is the
campaign's record of what each planner run, batch, wave and module did and cost. It is
filled from `templates/translate/dashboard.template.md`, an audit's from
`templates/audit/dashboard.template.md`, and keeps the template's format exactly.
When an adopted Crustify change adds a table or a column to the template, it is
added to the dashboard on the working branch before the next batch launches: a batch
fills the rows of the tables in place, and never adds one.

It is tracked in the campaign's tree, so every agent's worktree holds a copy, and it is
filled as the work lands rather than at the end. Each figure is measured once, where it is
produced: no suite or scan is rerun only to record one.

## 2. Cells

The dashboard's cells fall into three kinds, by when their figures can be known.

### 2.1 Landing cells

The cells measured on the tree a landing commits:

- for a batch, under the route its items' `kind` selects, as
  [`task-schema`](../../artifacts/task-schema/SKILL.md)'s Routes section gives it: its rows
  in that route's `Batches`, tests, `Batches: safety audit` and `Batches: API stability` tables, and for a review batch in
  `Batches — review: PoC + reports`, each placed in module, wave and batch order under
  its `pass`, and for a module pass, which spans both routes, in `Module passes`; those
  tables' `Σ` rows; and the `Coverage stats` table and the Overview's LoC
  line;
- for a planner run, its row in `Planning`, but for its usage cells.

They are filled in the landing's last commit, and measured against the integration branch
tip it was rebased onto: coverage as [`testing-builds`](../../verification/testing/builds/SKILL.md)'s Coverage section measures
it, the safety audit columns as the changes in the dashboard's Safety audit metrics, and
the API stability columns as the changes to the API of the landing's items are classified. A
rebase that conflicts in the dashboard keeps every row both sides added, and the landing's
cells, `Σ` rows included, are measured again where the gates its rebase reruns cover them;
the others stand as measured on the batch's base.

An integration merge, and any merge of one branch into another, keeps every row both
sides added, and settles the rest so: an additive `Σ` cell is the sum over the merged
rows, ours plus theirs less the merge base's, and so are the Overview's `Rust LoC`
figures; a usage `Σ` cell, its per-unit cells included, sums only the rows that carry
usage, so that it is filled again with theirs; a coverage `Σ` cell, and the Overview's
`C LoC`, are the later landing's; and `Coverage stats` takes the merged suites' counts,
with the later landing's percentages until a gate measures the merged tree, which the
merge commit's message says. A table or section the template holds once is kept once,
with the rows of every copy, whether or not the merge conflicts there, and the merged
dashboard is checked for repeated headings before it is committed.

### 2.2 Usage cells
## 3. Records

Every run's `task.json` records how its agent ran: its backend, billing, model proxy and
the arguments its CLI was given, and, once it starts, its `session_id`, which ties the run
to its session. The session's transcript, which its CLI keeps by session id, is the
agent's full log and the source of its accounting. An agent spawned as a subagent of
another session has no session of its own: its session id is `agent-<agent id>`, the
name its host gives its transcript, under the spawning session's `subagents/`.

A transcript is copied into crustify's home, as `transcripts/<session id>.jsonl`, as soon
as its agent ends, because the CLIs move and prune their own files. Its usage is derived
from the copy, as [`usage`](../usage/SKILL.md) describes, with the backend and model proxy its
`task.json` names.

An evolution review is a run like any other: its `task.json` sits in its artifact dir, and
its transcript is collected and priced the same way, its cost counted with the sessions that
orchestrate the campaign and recorded, with its tokens and wall time, in its proposal's
Review section, so that what each review bought can be weighed against its cost.

The sessions that orchestrate the campaign are collected the same way: at the start of each session, the
transcripts of the sessions before it. A resumed session keeps its id while its transcript
grows: its transcript is copied again after each run, replacing the earlier copy. The
records, transcripts and rates stay in crustify's home.

## 4. Cost and time

another session has no session of its own: its session id is `agent-<agent id>`, the
name its host gives its transcript, under the spawning session's `subagents/`.

as its agent ends, because the CLIs move and prune their own files. Its usage is derived
from the copy, as [`usage`](../usage/SKILL.md) describes, with the backend and model proxy its
`task.json` names.

An evolution review is a run like any other: its `task.json` sits in its artifact dir, and
its transcript is collected and priced the same way, its cost counted with the sessions that
orchestrate the campaign and recorded, with its tokens and wall time, in its proposal's
Review section, so that what each review bought can be weighed against its cost.

The sessions that orchestrate the campaign are collected the same way: at the start of each session, the
transcripts of the sessions before it. A resumed session keeps its id while its transcript
grows: its transcript is copied again after each run, replacing the earlier copy. The
records, transcripts and rates stay in crustify's home.

## 4. Landing

A batch lands its commits on the integration branch it was given, which is never checked
out. Before committing, the diff is checked to contain no unrelated work. A commit carries
no trailer but the co-author trailers of the campaign's [identity](#6-identity), and its
subject says what it does and which run made it. A batch's names its module's file and its
objective and ends with its run's id, as `refs.c: wrap 12 items (wave-3/batch-1/run-2)`,
and its body lists the items it translated by their anchors' paths, as
`fn::git_reference_lookup`, one per line; a review batch's two commits name what they file
and what they fix the same way, and a planner run's subject ends with its run's id. A
progress commit is `progress: wave-<index>`, and an integration's merge, in the campaign's
repository and on the fork's `main`, `integrate <module>`, the module written as
[`modules-schema`](../../artifacts/modules-schema/SKILL.md) writes it.

The landing operation is a local push of the batch's tip to the integration branch through
the repository's Git common directory, which accepts only a fast-forward. A direct ref
update is no substitute: its compare-and-swap form makes the update atomic, but does not
enforce that the new commit descends from the expected old commit.

### 4.1 The landing lock

An integration branch is landed on by one batch at a time, under its landing lock: an
exclusive `flock` on a file in the Git common directory, named after the branch with its
`refs/heads/` prefix dropped, so that every worktree of the repository sees the same lock:

```text
$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/crustify/landing/<integration branch>.lock
```

A batch whose validated work is committed on its own branch takes the lock and holds it
until its landing has succeeded:

1. it acquires the lock, waiting while another batch holds it;
2. it rebases only its own branch onto the current integration branch, once: nothing else
   lands while it holds the lock;
3. it resolves any conflict the rebase raises and runs again, on the rebased tree, the
   gates that could catch a regression of the integration, as
   [`testing-gates`](../../verification/testing/gates/SKILL.md)'s Regressions section describes, fixing what fails;
4. it pushes the fast-forward, which nothing can reject; and
5. it releases the lock.

A conflict or a failing gate is resolved under the lock rather than after releasing it, so
that the branch cannot move again in between and no batch rebases twice.

The waiter blocks in `flock` itself, so the kernel wakes it the moment the lock is released,
and nothing polls. Once it holds the lock, it hands the locked descriptor to a process of
its own, detached from the shell that started it and bound to the lifetime of the agent's
CLI: a `flock` lock belongs to the open file, so that process keeps it after the command
that took it exits, until that CLI ends, however it ends, and the kernel releases it. The
holder records itself beside the lock, in `<integration branch>.lock.holder`, as its own pid
and the CLI's. A waiter bounds each wait, to stay within the time a single command may run,
and waits again when it expires. For example, with `$CLI_PID` the agent CLI's pid, found by
walking up the shell's parent processes:
<!-- TODO: this procedure must run exactly so: it belongs in a script beside this skill,
documented by its `--help`, as `authoring` describes. -->

```bash
lock="$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/crustify/landing/<integration branch>.lock"
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$lock")"
# wait in the kernel, up to 10 minutes per command; then hand the lock to a detached holder
sh -c '
  exec 9>"$1"
  flock -w 600 9 || exit 1
  setsid sh -c "echo \"\$\$ $2\" > \"$1.holder\"; exec tail --pid=$2 -f /dev/null" 9>&9 &
' sh "$lock" "$CLI_PID"
# release, once the push has succeeded
holder=$(cut -d' ' -f1 "$lock.holder"); rm -f "$lock.holder"; kill "$holder"
```

The holder file is removed before the holder is ended, while the lock is still held, so
that a release never removes the next holder's record.

The lock has no timeout: the regression gates it covers vary in length. A holder that has
stopped making progress keeps it until its agent is ended. That releases it where the
agent ran in a CLI of its own. An agent that shared its CLI with others leaves its holder
running: the holder is then ended as a release ends it, by the pid its record names, the
record removed first. The batch is then run again, as any failed batch is.

### 4.2 Commits

Every landing is a fast-forward, so an integration branch is linear, and each batch's
commits are one unbroken run of it, ending at its branch's tip and starting after the wave
base or the tip of the batch that landed before it: the commits its branch reaches and
neither the wave base nor the wave's other landed batches reach, oldest first, which
become the batch's `commits` in `schedule.json`.

The integration branch is never reset, force-updated or moved backward, and nothing is
pushed to a remote. The worktree stays after landing, until it is purged as [Lifecycle](#5-lifecycle)
describes.
<!-- TODO: when the working and shipping branches, and a wrapper's, are pushed to their
remotes is not specified yet, though a wrapper's reuse and a Git-pinned dependency need
it. -->

### 4.3 Promotion

### 5.5 Batches

A batch's branch and worktree, forked from its wave branch's tip, are created before it
launches, with its run dir, as [`layout`](../layout/SKILL.md) describes. The gitignored state its tree needs and does
not build itself, such as shared analysis databases, is symlinked from the base checkout,
and its `c/` is a worktree of the base checkout's submodule at the commit the superproject
records, since no batch changes the C.
Once the batch has landed, its worktree is purged; its branch stays until its commits are
recorded in `schedule.json`, since they are derived from it, as
[Landing](#4-landing) describes. A batch that fails keeps its branch and worktree for
inspection; they are removed before it is run again, which forks them anew.

## 6. Identity

Every commit of a campaign, in its repository and its wrappers', is authored and committed
as Crustify, whose GitHub account is `crustify-ai` and whose git identity is
`crustify <crustify@berkeley.edu>`, whatever the repository's git configuration says,
unless the settings' `identity` answer names another: an author and any co-authors, each
as `Name <email>`. The author named there then authors and commits every commit, and each
message ends with one `Co-Authored-By:` trailer per co-author and no other, none that an
agent's host suggests included.

The identity is passed explicitly, as configuration on the command line, to every command
that writes a commit, a rebase, a merge and a cherry-pick as much as a commit, since the
host may have no git identity of its own.
## 5. Unsafe code

Every unsafe block carries a specific, falsifiable `// SAFETY:` comment: the invariant the
operation relies on, and why it holds on every path that reaches it. Native Rust APIs are
safe unless their caller obligation cannot be expressed in the type system; an `unsafe fn`
documents that obligation in its `# Safety` section.

Unsafe code sits only in a module's unsafe regions and in the raw bindings, as the
[conventions](../conventions/SKILL.md)' Unsafe regions section describes. A region that
holds unsafe code of its own takes `unsafe_code` back where it is declared, as
`#[expect(unsafe_code, reason = "<what it reaches>")] mod ffi_import { … }`, so that the
expectation fails once the region holds none; and so does each test suite and unit-test
module that holds unsafe code. A region whose only unsafe code a macro of another crate
expands takes none: the lint does not see that code, and the expectation would fail. A
module with no region carries `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, which no item within it can take
back.

### `libgit2/deps/llhttp/api.c` wave 194 batch 4: the lifecycle, the name functions and the dispatchers

api.c's last `port` batch, the `symbol` route of waves 195 and 196: 32 items in
`src/libgit2/deps/llhttp/api.rs`. `fn::llhttp_init` is `ParserMut::init(ParserType,
Option<SettingsRef<'static>>)`, over `reinit`, `set_parser_type` and `set_settings`;
`fn::llhttp_reset` is `ParserMut::reset()`, which keeps the type byte, the table, `data` and the
lenient flags across `reinit`, so a parser of both kinds keeps the type its first message
settled; `fn::llhttp_finish` is `ParserMut::finish() -> Result<(), FinishError>`, where
`FinishError` is `InvalidEofState` (with C's reason `"Invalid EOF state"`) or
`on_message_complete`'s own non-zero value, `HPE_PAUSED` included, neither kept as the parser's
error, as C keeps neither. A parser with an error finishes at once, as C's does, and a finish
state no `llhttp_finish` names panics where C aborts. `fn::llhttp_settings_init` keeps batch 2's
`Settings::new()`, now native, the zeroed table its `memset` leaves; its anchor moved from
`Wraps` to `Replaces`. The name functions `llhttp_errno_name`, `llhttp_method_name` and
`llhttp_status_name` are each a `switch` of the cases batch 3's generators stand for, so they
are ported onto `Errno::constant_name`, `Method::map_string` and `Status::map_string`, which
carry a third anchor each (`crustify/evolution/port-onto-an-existing-accessor`, with this
evidence); their `default: abort()` no enum reaches.

The 23 dispatchers are one table, `with_dispatchers!`, from which the native methods, the
region's slot reads and the gateway's exports are made. `mac::CALLBACK_MAYBE` and
`mac::SPAN_CALLBACK_MAYBE` are the private `callback_maybe(EventSlot)` and
`span_callback_maybe(SpanSlot, &[u8])`, the stringified `#NAME` a per-slot `&'static CStr` made
at compile time; each `fn::llhttp__on_<slot>` is the public `ParserMut::on_<slot>()` or
`on_<slot>(&[u8])` over them, returning C's `int`, which `llhttp.c`'s port will call. A
dispatcher reads the table the parser holds through `ffi_import` alone: the region maps a slot
to its field and calls what it holds with the parser, so that a C table, whose callbacks read
`data`, is still only called with its own parser. The dispatchers being safe,
`set_settings_ptr`'s and `set_data`'s contracts now say that the callbacks they vouch for may be
called at any time while the parser holds them, in any order, with any run. `reset` restores
`data` and `settings` through `ffi_import`'s `reinit_keeping_context`, and the type byte, as C
stores an unnamed `llhttp_type_t`, through `set_parser_type_byte`. `init` and `reset` panic, as
`reinit` does, from a callback of their parser's own parse; the dispatchers and `finish` do
not need to, since they leave where the parse stands. libc's `abort` and `memset` keep their
`std` route: the zeroed value for `memset`, `std::process::abort` in `llhttp_init`'s gateway,
which cannot fail, and a panic where `llhttp_finish` aborts, reported as `HPE_INTERNAL` by its
export, as `llhttp_execute`'s is.

The gateway gains 25 exports under `ffi-export-deps-llhttp-api-c`, every function C outside
api.c calls: `llhttp_init` (`httpparser.h`'s macro, in `httpclient.c`), `llhttp_finish`
(`httpparser.c`) and the 23 dispatchers (`llhttp.c`). `llhttp_init` and `llhttp_finish` are
checked against their raw bindings. No header declares the dispatchers, which `llhttp.c`
declares for itself, so they have no raw binding: each is checked against a function-pointer
type transcribed from `llhttp.c`'s prototype, and the `equiv` tests reach api.c's C through an
`extern` block of their own (`crustify/evolution/exports-without-a-header-declaration`). The
raw bindings gain `llhttp_finish`'s enum, the `HTTP_FINISH_*` states `finish` matches. The five
others have no C caller outside api.c and are not exported. With every export of the module in
place, the link check of the task message ran: private builds under `crustify/tmp/linkcheck/`
whose archive copy lacks `api.c.o` (211 objects), named by `CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR`, with the
feature on. On `plain`, `lib` (858, the gateway's six `unit_priv` tests among them), `ub_safe`
785, `ub_unsafe` 134, `unit_pub` 156, `hidden_symbols` and the doctests (92 and 387) pass,
`nm` showing the exports defined and api.c's other symbols, such as `llhttp__debug`, absent; on
`asan-ubsan` the same, but for the known nightly `compile_fail` snapshots and `CommitBuilder`
doctest. `equiv` cannot link there by design: it calls the 19 api.c functions that have no
export. Two `ub_unsafe` fixtures, batch 0's and batch 5's, called `llhttp_settings_init` and
failed to link too; they now build the zeroed table themselves (`export-link-check`, with this
evidence).

Tests: 2 `unit_priv` (each span slot's reason, and `c_str`'s refusal) and 6 more in the
gateway's region, under the feature (the span from `p` to `endp`, an empty span NULL or
dangling, a span export's `-1`, an event export reading neither pointer, `llhttp_init` over
garbage storage and an unnamed type, `llhttp_finish`'s codes), 14 `unit_pub` (`init` over a
used parser, `reset`'s kept and cleared fields and a settled type, `finish` from each state, its
callback's values and its refusal, every dispatcher against its slot, with no table or slot,
the span dispatchers' `HPE_USER` and reasons and any other value handed back), 2 `ub_safe`
(`init` and `reset` refused inside their parser's parse; callbacks that dispatch to and finish
their parser mid-parse), 4 `equiv` (`init`, `reset` and `finish` against `llhttp_init`,
`llhttp_reset` and `llhttp_finish` from six states with `data` and lenient flags set, the whole
parser compared and the next message parsed by both; the 23 dispatchers against api.c's over
five tables and none) and 3 doctests. The dispatchers' tests run one table over all 23, as one
pattern. No `ub_unsafe` suite: no public `unsafe fn` is added. llhttp has no C tests in the
tree. `new_and_default_are_empty_tables` no longer calls C and runs under Miri.

Coverage: `run.sh` on this tree after its rebase onto `f58d38aa9`, read with `report.py` from
the scratch tree's `src/libgit2`, the unit column merging `lib` and `unit_pub`; the pp cells
are against batch 5's figures for that tip. Worklist: `api.rs` 182 of 187 lines, 38 of 39
functions and 221 of 227 regions, the misses `c_str`, which only the compiler evaluated, and
which two `unit_priv` tests added after the measurement call at run time; the gateway is
compiled out. `api.c` moves to 267 of its 283 lines and 54 of 55 functions under `equiv`,
`llhttp__debug` the one left (batch 3's note). Of the parser's states the tests reach fresh,
reading, between messages, paused, upgrade-paused, failed and settled on a request, and every
transition `init`, `reset` and `finish` make from them; of `finish`, its three states and one
it refuses. The Overview's Rust LoC moves by ffimap's `code.loc.total` (`+148`) and
`code.tests.loc.total` (`+808`); `ported symbols` counts the 32 and `wrapped symbols` loses
`llhttp_settings_init`. `+LoC` leaves out the regenerated `bindings.rs` (`+4`). The `loc` cell
is wavefront's `query dag --loc`.

The safety audit scan (ffimap `9aa2ef1`, flags as batch 5's, the export feature on) is compared
with batch 5's recorded scan of the tip. `raw→std` `+2` is the region's `as_ref` of the table
and the gateway's span slice; `raw deref` `+1` the type byte's write; `FFI calls` `+1` the two
calls through a table's slots less `llhttp_settings_init`'s; of the 42 new unsafe blocks, 35
are the exports' and left out of the cell, five the region's and two the gateway's `span`
helper, less `Settings::new`'s. The boundary scan's sites hold none in the changeset: those in
the llhttp files are batch 0's `data` and `settings` accessors. `ffimap api` against the tip
(nightly `2026-10-08`, ffibox's with private items): `fn::llhttp_settings_init` is `kept`, its
anchor moved `Wraps→Replaces`, the other 29 public items `new`, and the two macro ports,
private, `missing`. Unattributed, `api` is new (`FinishError`) and `sys::libgit2` gains the
three `HTTP_FINISH_*`, but reads `changed`: the new `llhttp_finish` alias shares the function's
path, which `ffimap api` keys as one item (`crustify/evolution/ffimap-api-namespaces-share-a-path`,
with a reproducer); the function is unchanged.

Gates, on the tree rebased onto `f58d38aa9`, the wave branch's tip: formatted (nightly
rustfmt; `build.rs`'s diff is the base's), and `clippy --workspace --all-targets` passes with
warnings denied with the export feature off and on. The whole workspace passes on `plain`
(`lib` 854 and 1 ignored, `equiv` 553, `ub_safe` 785, `ub_unsafe` 135, `unit_pub` 156,
`hidden_symbols` 1, doctests 92 merged and 387 standalone), and on `coverage` but for the known
`CommitBuilder` doctest. Every llhttp test passes under ASan+UBSan, the doctests included.
Miri passes the batch's Rust-only tests (6 `unit_pub`, 2 `unit_priv`, and 5 of the gateway's
with the feature on); each marked test of the module's api files was run alone and stops at
`llhttp__internal_init`, or for `debug_trace`'s at C's `stderr`. TSan has no obligation: no
`Send` or `Sync` claim and no thread; BSan was not run, as nothing here is expected to trigger
it and the settings' `sanitizers` answer reserves it. The raw bindings changed, so the crate
was packaged (`--no-verify --exclude-lockfile`, 697 files) and built alone in bundled mode with

`plain` installs on `OPENSSL_ROOT_DIR`, `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` and `PKG_CONFIG_PATH`. Usage cells

### `libgit2/deps/llhttp/api.c` integration: the switch from C

The campaign's third switch, run by `modules/libgit2/deps/llhttp/api.c/integration/run-1` on the
module's branch, after the merge of the working branch (`a4335ab7a`): `21c5c5f47`, and the fork's
`c54c0c180`. It followed the procedure of `utf8.c`'s and `opt.c`'s switches
(`crustify/evolution/module-switch-procedure`) with their scripts unchanged. The export feature
`ffi-export-deps-llhttp-api-c` is deleted, so `api.rs`'s gateway compiles from now on, and its
eight `unit_priv` tests run in `lib`. No export feature is left. The remaining C calls the 31
exports: `transports/httpparser.c` calls `llhttp_execute`, `llhttp_finish`,
`llhttp_get_error_pos` and `llhttp_resume_after_upgrade`, `httpparser.h`'s macros, which
`httpclient.c` expands, call `llhttp_init`, `llhttp_pause`, `llhttp_resume` and
`llhttp_get_error_reason`, and `llhttp.c`'s generated parser calls the 23 `llhttp__on_*`
dispatchers. The raw bindings of the eight functions stay and reach the exports. The dispatchers
have no header declaration and no raw binding. The 23 functions bound without an export go with
their allowlist entries: the seven getters, the three name functions, `llhttp_settings_init`,
`llhttp_reset`, `llhttp_set_error_reason` and the ten lenient setters. Only api.c's equivalence
tests called them, and `bindings.rs` was regenerated without them. Removing them changes the
crate's raw API, `sys::libgit2`, as the porting workflow's switch has it; the safe API does not
change. The types stay for the layouts `httpparser.c` and `llhttp.c` build and read.
`deps/llhttp/api.c` leaves `c/` on the local `fork/main` as `integrate deps/llhttp/api.c`,
which is not pushed. `llhttp.h` stays for `llhttp.c`, `http.c` and the HTTP client.
`deps/llhttp/CMakeLists.txt` globs its sources and is unchanged; its
`set_source_files_properties(api.c http.c llhttp.c …)` names the removed file, and CMake ignores
it. The module has no tied C test. The doc comment that counted nine functions C calls now says
eight.

The module's 21 `equiv` tests are retired with the C they compared (`tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/api.rs`
and its `mod api;`). Each calls C, api.c's own or `llhttp.c`'s parse through it, and carries the
Miri `calls C` marker, so none is carried over. The module pass (`wave-194/batch-7`'s `misc`
report) maps each to the unit tests that keep its behaviour. What none keeps is the
differential itself. The parser's private state was compared byte for byte with C's from six
states, and the lenient setters were shown to read any nonzero `int` as true. Once the C is gone,
nothing is left to compare with. `tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/llhttp.rs` stays: it compares
`llhttp.c`'s port with its C, whose parse now runs over the Rust dispatchers.

The Rust side landed before the variants were built: every variant's build runs
`rust-staticlib.sh`, which checks the committed bindings and compiles the gateway (proposal's
item 10). The variants were rebuilt as `crustify/builds.gen3` from `c54c0c180` with
`build-variants.sh`, at 12 jobs each so that the five stayed within the host's 64. This
worktree's `crustify/builds` links to gen3, and gen2 was left untouched. Each archive holds 210
objects where gen2's held 211, `api.c.o` gone. In every variant, `libgit2.so`, `git2` and
`libgit2_tests` define the 31 exports and none of api.c's 23 other functions. `addr2line` puts
`llhttp_execute` at `api.rs:1634`. Each variant passed its smoke test (`util_tests -sutf8`,
`git2 --version`). `libgit2.so`'s dynamic symbol table defines the same 907 symbols. It now
holds 6747 local Rust functions where gen2's held 6337 (proposal's item 9).

Gates, over gen3 from `end-gates` snapshots at 64 jobs. The workspace is formatted, and `clippy
--workspace --all-targets` passes with warnings denied. Plain passes the whole workspace:
`lib` 901 and 1 ignored, `equiv` 532, `ub_safe` 796, `ub_unsafe` 144, `unit_pub` 218,
`hidden_symbols` 1, doctests 101 and 397. ASan+UBSan and TSan pass it but for the known nightly
failures: the 9 `compile_fail` snapshots, the six `checkout_*`,
`diff_parse_options_no_raw_conversion`, `odb_options_no_raw_conversion` and
`progress_callback_not_send`, and the `CommitBuilder` doctest (E0624). Neither printed a
sanitizer report. The gateway's eight tests pass on plain, ASan+UBSan and TSan, the first time
under TSan. Miri passes every binary: `lib` 441, `ub_safe` 212, `unit_pub` 141, `equiv` 38,
`ub_unsafe` 26, the rest marked. The gateway's tests are among them: six pass, and
`llhttp_init_initialises_storage_and_stores_what_c_passes` and
`llhttp_execute_keeps_an_empty_runs_error_pos_at_data` are marked `calls C`. The remaining C
tests ran over the link with the Rust through `c-tests.sh`. Plain, ASan+UBSan and TSan give 3443
passed and 55 skipped of 3498, coverage 3444 and 54, each the baseline's record. Under TSan, the
same 10 suites as the baseline's report the C's lock-order inversions and races, and no case
fails; no report has a Rust frame. `ctest` passes both targets on plain, ASan+UBSan and
coverage. Under TSan it fails `offline` on those reports alone, 49 lock-order inversions and
glibc's `tzset` race, as at the two switches before. BSan was rebuilt and not run, as the
settings' `sanitizers` answer has it.

No offline C test drives the HTTP client, and the baseline disables the online suites. So this
switch checked the exports through libgit2's own C over a smart-HTTP remote on localhost:
`crustify/scripts/http-remote.py`, `git http-backend` behind an HTTP/1.1 front with persistent
connections, and `crustify/scripts/http-gate.sh` (proposal's item 11). The front frames each
response by its path: `Content-Length`, chunked in 1, 7, 4096 and 65536-byte chunks, chunked
with chunk extensions, close-delimited, or a header block llhttp refuses. One remote asks for
Basic credentials. The variant's `git2` cloned `testrepo.git` and a three-commit repository of
the source revision's tree through the first three framings, each clone's refs, HEAD, checkout
and `fsck --connectivity-only` checked. It also ran four clones that fail: close-delimited ("could
not read refs from remote repository"), malformed ("http parser error: Invalid header token",
the reason read through `llhttp_get_error_reason`), 404 and 401. Through each of the first three
framings, `libgit2_tests -sonline::push -sonline::clone::credentials` ran against the guarded
remote with `GITTEST_REMOTE_URL`, as libgit2's CI runs `auth_clone_and_push`, and passed 23 with
1 skipped. Gen2's C and gen3's Rust give the same `results.txt` on plain, ASan+UBSan and TSan, and
gen3's coverage variant gives it too: every outcome, every clone's refs, and the requests each
remote answered, by method, framing and status. No run printed a sanitizer report. On the
coverage variant, the run called 24 of the 31 exports, the chunk-extension dispatchers
included, and covered `api.rs`'s 128 of 175 lines and 31 of 44 functions. The seven it never
calls are `on_url` and `on_method` and their `_complete`s, which only a request parse calls,
`on_reset` and `llhttp_resume_after_upgrade`, which need pipelined or upgraded messages, and
`llhttp_finish`, which libgit2 calls only when the socket ends inside a body. The gateway's
`unit_priv` tests call six of them: `each_dispatcher_export_calls_its_own_slot` calls every
dispatcher and `llhttp_finish_returns_cs_codes` calls `llhttp_finish`. None calls
`llhttp_resume_after_upgrade`, whose body is `ParserMut::resume_after_upgrade` in a `barrier`;
`unit_pub`'s `resume_after_upgrade_clears_only_an_upgrades_pause` tests that method. The results are kept in the run dir
(`http-gate-results.txt`), for the switches of `http.c` and `llhttp.c` to compare with.

`c/` changed, so the crate was packaged as `package-gate-procedure` has it, with the workspace's
Git patch of ffibox, as at `opt.c`'s switch. It has 695 files, `api.c` out, and builds alone in
bundled mode, where `llhttp.c`'s dispatchers resolve to the Rust. Its `lib` tests: 843 pass, the
gateway's eight among them. The other 58 need the fixture repositories of `c/tests/resources`,
as at the two switches before.

From the switch on, the module's coverage is its Rust's, and the C figures lose `api.c`'s 283
lines. This run did not measure the workspace's coverage. What this switch shows the procedure
lacks is added to `crustify/evolution/module-switch-procedure` (items 10 to 13). The review
reproducer that enables the deleted feature (`wave-194/batch-7/equiv/execute-export-moves-an-empty-runs-error-pos`)
is left as it is, reproducing at the commit its report names. Usage cells are the assistant's.

# Builds in this repository run the raw bindings in campaign mode, against the `plain`
# variant unless CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT names another, or is set empty to build as a
# dependent would (crustify's `bindgen` skill, Build modes).
[env]
CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT = "plain"
# pcre2-sys links the PCRE2 that pkg-config finds, else builds its vendored copy, which would
# shadow the side campaign's for libgit2's C too: point it at the variant's install
# (crustify/evolution/bundled-pcre2-shadows-the-side-campaign). cargo-variant.sh sets
# another variant's, which this does not override. The install is reached as the variant's
# build found it, from crustify/builds/plain, which a worktree or a gate snapshot links to the

#!/bin/bash
# Run cargo against one crustify prebuild of libgit2, instrumenting Rust to match.
#
#   crustify/scripts/cargo-variant.sh <variant> <cargo subcommand> [args...]
#
# <variant> is a `variants` key of crustify/artifacts/build.json: plain, coverage, asan-ubsan,
# tsan or bsan. Each variant uses its own target dir under target/.
# The safe crate's build script, in campaign mode, links the variant's static archive (its
# `static` in build.json) into each test binary, so the C runs under the instrumentation the
# Rust is built with here, one runtime serving both. Set CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR to a private build
# of the variant, which carries the same archive, to link it instead of the shared one.
set -euo pipefail
variant=${1:?usage: cargo-variant.sh <variant> <cargo subcommand> [args...]}
shift
here=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)
host=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
export CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT=$variant
export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=${CARGO_TARGET_DIR:-$here/target/$variant}
# pcre2-sys links the variant's side-campaign PCRE2, the one libgit2's C links, rather than
# building its vendored copy, which would shadow it in every test binary. The side campaigns'
# clones sit where the variant's build found their installs, beside the repository whose
# crustify/builds holds it (build.json's configure takes them from `$PWD/../../../..` in
# crustify/builds/<variant>): resolved physically through crustify/builds, which a worktree or
# a gate snapshot links to that repository's, so that every checkout finds the same ones.
side=$(realpath -m "$here/crustify/builds/$variant/../../../..")
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="$side/pcre2-bindings/crustify/builds/$variant/install/lib/pkgconfig${PKG_CONFIG_PATH:+:$PKG_CONFIG_PATH}"
cd "$here"
# The nightly the workspace pins, for the sanitizers that need it.
nightly=$(sed -n 's/^nightly = "\(.*\)"$/\1/p' Cargo.toml)
# Cargo's own flags must come before a `--`, which hands the rest to the test binaries.
pre=() post=()
for arg in "$@"; do
  if [ ${#post[@]} -gt 0 ] || [ "$arg" = -- ]; then post+=("$arg"); else pre+=("$arg"); fi
done
case $variant in
  plain)
    exec cargo "$@" ;;
  coverage)
    # Source-based coverage on the pinned nightly, against the variant's clang-instrumented C,
    # which each test binary links statically, so that rustc's profiler runtime counts both;
    # crustify/scripts/coverage/ measures the suites as the testing spec's Coverage section does.
    export RUSTFLAGS="${RUSTFLAGS:-} -C instrument-coverage"
    export RUSTDOCFLAGS="${RUSTDOCFLAGS:-} -C instrument-coverage"
    export LLVM_PROFILE_FILE=${LLVM_PROFILE_FILE:-$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/profraw/%p-%m.profraw}
    exec cargo "+$nightly" "${pre[@]}" --target $host "${post[@]}" ;;
  asan-ubsan)
    export RUSTFLAGS="${RUSTFLAGS:-} -Zsanitizer=address -Cforce-frame-pointers=yes"
    export RUSTDOCFLAGS="${RUSTDOCFLAGS:-} -Zsanitizer=address"
    export ASAN_OPTIONS=${ASAN_OPTIONS:-detect_leaks=1:abort_on_error=1}
    export UBSAN_OPTIONS=${UBSAN_OPTIONS:-print_stacktrace=1:halt_on_error=1}
    exec cargo "+$nightly" "${pre[@]}" --target $host "${post[@]}" ;;
  tsan)
    export RUSTFLAGS="${RUSTFLAGS:-} -Zsanitizer=thread"
    export RUSTDOCFLAGS="${RUSTDOCFLAGS:-} -Zsanitizer=thread"
    # glibc's tzset locks what TSan cannot see: see tsan.supp.
    export TSAN_OPTIONS=${TSAN_OPTIONS:-halt_on_error=1:suppressions=$here/crustify/scripts/tsan.supp}
    exec cargo "+$nightly" "${pre[@]}" -Zbuild-std --target $host "${post[@]}" ;;
  bsan)
    # trybuild's nested cargo build does not finish under BorrowSanitizer, and the
    # compile-fail suite is a compile-time check the plain variant already runs.
    # Under parallel test threads BorrowSanitizer's GC can take longer than its default
    # 10 s hang threshold to bring every thread to a safepoint, and then aborts; give it
    # 120 s rather than serialize the tests.
    export BSAN_OPTIONS=${BSAN_OPTIONS:-gc_hang_threshold_ms=120000}
    if [ "${1:-}" = test ]; then
      case " $* " in
        *" -- "*) exec cargo bsan "$@" --skip compile_fail ;;
        *) exec cargo bsan "$@" -- --skip compile_fail ;;
      esac
    fi
    exec cargo bsan "$@" ;;
  *)
    echo "unknown variant: $variant" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

#!/bin/bash
# Drive libgit2's HTTP client through a variant's own C, over a smart-HTTP remote on localhost
# (crustify's testing-gates skill, Regressions: a module's switch, for a module whose exports
# the HTTP client reaches, which no offline C test does; crustify/evolution/module-switch-procedure).
#
#   http-gate.sh <variant dir> <out dir>
#
# <variant dir> is a built variant, crustify/builds.gen<n>/<variant>, with its `git2` and
# `libgit2_tests`; nothing is written into it. Two remotes are started from
# crustify/scripts/http-remote.py over scratch repositories under <out dir>/remotes, one open
# and one asking for Basic credentials (foo:bar), each serving every framing it offers
# (Content-Length, chunked, chunked with extensions, close-delimited, malformed):
#
# 1. the variant's `git2 clone` of testrepo.git (c/tests/resources) and of a three-commit
#    repository of the generation's c/ tree at a fixed commit, through the Content-Length and
#    chunked framings, and clones that fail: through the close-delimited framing, which
#    libgit2 does not read to its end, through a response llhttp refuses, of a missing
#    repository (404), and of the guarded remote without credentials (401); each clone's exit
#    status, refs, HEAD, checked-out tree and `git fsck --connectivity-only` outcome, or its
#    error;
# 2. the variant's `libgit2_tests -sonline::push -sonline::clone::credentials`, libgit2's own
#    C tests of a push and a clone over GITTEST_REMOTE_URL, against the guarded remote with
#    foo:bar, through the Content-Length and chunked framings: its TAP tally.
#
# <out dir>/results.txt is one line per case, free of times, ports and paths, so that two
# generations' results compare with `diff`; every process's output is kept beside it, and each
# line counts the sanitizer reports that process printed (`reports=`). The exit status is 0
# when every clone that should succeed did and every suite passed, 1 otherwise.
set -uo pipefail
usage='usage: http-gate.sh <variant dir> <out dir>'
d=$(cd -P "${1:?$usage}" && pwd) || exit 2
out=${2:?$usage}
here=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
c=$(cd -P "$d/../c" && pwd) || { echo "http-gate.sh: no generation c/ beside $d" >&2; exit 2; }
[ -x "$d/git2" ] && [ -x "$d/libgit2_tests" ] || { echo "http-gate.sh: $d has no git2 or libgit2_tests" >&2; exit 2; }
rm -rf "$out"
mkdir -p "$out"
out=$(cd -P "$out" && pwd)
export LLVM_PROFILE_FILE=${LLVM_PROFILE_FILE:-/dev/null}
export GIT_AUTHOR_DATE='2026-01-01T00:00:00Z' GIT_COMMITTER_DATE='2026-01-01T00:00:00Z'
# big.git's tree: the campaign's source revision, which every generation's c/ holds.
big_tip=0551dfd4a
framings=(length chunked chunked-ext)
status=0
results=$out/results.txt
: >"$results"
reports() { grep -cE 'WARNING: ThreadSanitizer|ERROR: AddressSanitizer|ERROR: LeakSanitizer|runtime error:' "$@" 2>/dev/null | awk -F: '{s+=$NF} END {print s+0}'; }

# The remotes' repositories.
r=$out/remotes
mkdir -p "$r/open" "$r/guarded"
git clone -q --bare "$c/tests/resources/testrepo.git" "$r/open/testrepo.git"
# big.git: the source revision's tree as three commits, the second removing src/ and the
# third restoring it, each with a fixed author and date, so that its ids are every run's.
mkdir -p "$r/src"
git -C "$c" archive "$big_tip" | tar -x -C "$r/src"
(
  cd "$r/src" && git init -q -b main . &&
    export GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=crustify GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=crustify@berkeley.edu \
      GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=crustify GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=crustify@berkeley.edu &&
    git add -A && git commit -q -m tree &&
    git rm -q -r src && git commit -q -m 'without src' &&
    git revert --no-edit HEAD >/dev/null
)
git clone -q --bare "$r/src" "$r/open/big.git"
rm -rf "$r/src"
for f in "${framings[@]}"; do git init -q --bare "$r/guarded/push-$f.git"; done
git clone -q --bare "$c/tests/resources/testrepo.git" "$r/guarded/testrepo.git"

pids=()
trap 'kill "${pids[@]}" 2>/dev/null' EXIT
python3 -I "$here/http-remote.py" "$r/open" "$out/open.port" --log "$out/open.log" 2>"$out/open.err" &
pids+=($!)
python3 -I "$here/http-remote.py" "$r/guarded" "$out/guarded.port" --auth foo:bar --log "$out/guarded.log" 2>"$out/guarded.err" &
pids+=($!)
for _ in $(seq 100); do [ -s "$out/open.port" ] && [ -s "$out/guarded.port" ] && break; sleep 0.1; done
open=http://127.0.0.1:$(cat "$out/open.port")
guarded=http://127.0.0.1:$(cat "$out/guarded.port")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""A smart-HTTP Git remote on localhost, for the C that drives libgit2's HTTP client.

    http-remote.py <root> <port file> [--auth USER:PASS] [--log FILE]

Serves the repositories under <root> through `git http-backend`, upload-pack and
receive-pack both, over HTTP/1.1 with persistent connections, so that libgit2's HTTP
client (src/libgit2/transports/httpclient.c over httpparser.c and llhttp) reads several
responses on one connection. It listens on 127.0.0.1 at a port the system picks, written to
<port file> once it accepts connections, and runs until killed.

The first component of a request's path picks how the response's body is framed, the rest
naming the repository under <root>, so that one remote serves every framing llhttp parses:

- `/length/<repo>`: a `Content-Length` body;
- `/chunked/<repo>`: `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, in chunks of 1, 7, 4096 and 65536 bytes
  in turn, so that a chunk's size line, its data and its end fall across reads;
- `/chunked-ext/<repo>`: chunked as above, every size line carrying chunk extensions
  (`;a=b;flag;q="x y"`), which llhttp's chunk-extension callbacks are called for;
- `/close/<repo>`: no length and no chunking, the body ending with the connection
  (`Connection: close`).
- `/malformed/<repo>`: a response whose header block llhttp refuses, a space in a header's
  name, so that the client reports the parser's error and its reason.

With `--auth`, every request without that user's Basic credentials is answered 401 with a
`WWW-Authenticate: Basic` challenge, a body and the connection kept, before the backend
runs. A path that names no repository is the backend's 404. Requests are logged to
`--log`, one line each, method, path and status, for the caller to compare.

Crustify's campaign check of a module whose exports libgit2's HTTP client reaches, at its
switch from C (crustify/evolution/module-switch-procedure): run it with `python3 -I`.
"""

import os

#!/bin/bash
# Build the safe crate's Rust static library for a variant's own C to link (crustify's
# porting-workflow skill, Builds): once a module has switched from C, the remaining C, its
# library, CLI and tests, reaches the module through the crate's exports, and its CMake
# build links this library (`LIBGIT2_RUST_LIBRARY`).
#
#   rust-staticlib.sh <variant> <archive>
#
# Run from the variant's build dir, configured and not yet built, as the first step of its
# `build` command in crustify/artifacts/build.json; <archive> is the library written,
# relative to the build dir, as its configure's `-DLIBGIT2_RUST_LIBRARY` names it. The crate
# is the one of the checkout this script belongs to, built as a `staticlib` on the dev
# profile, the campaign's tests' own, in campaign mode against this build dir
# (`CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR`) with `CRUSTIFY_STATICLIB` set, so that it reads the build's headers
# and configuration and links none of its C, and with the `bindgen` feature, so that the
# committed bindings are checked against them. Its Rust is instrumented as
# crustify/scripts/cargo-variant.sh instruments <variant>'s, so that one runtime serves the C
# and the Rust of every C consumer. Cargo's target dir is the build's own, `crustify/cargo`;
# the archive is replaced atomically, so that a link never reads a partial one.
set -euo pipefail
usage='usage: rust-staticlib.sh <variant> <archive>'
variant=${1:?$usage}
archive=${2:?$usage}
[ $# -eq 2 ] || { echo "$usage" >&2; exit 2; }
here=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)
host=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
[ -f CMakeCache.txt ] && [ -f build.ninja ] || {
  echo "rust-staticlib.sh: $PWD is not a configured CMake build with the Ninja generator" >&2
  exit 2
}
build=$(pwd -P)
case $archive in /*) ;; *) archive=$build/$archive ;; esac

export CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR=$build CRUSTIFY_STATICLIB=1
export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$build/crustify/cargo
crate=(-p libgit2-crustify --lib --locked --features bindgen)
bundled=
case $variant in
  plain)
    out=$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/debug
    "$here/crustify/scripts/cargo-variant.sh" "$variant" rustc "${crate[@]}" --crate-type staticlib ;;
  coverage|asan-ubsan|tsan)
    out=$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/$host/debug
    "$here/crustify/scripts/cargo-variant.sh" "$variant" rustc "${crate[@]}" --crate-type staticlib ;;
  bsan)
    # `cargo bsan` drives `build`, `run` and `test` only, and a `build` cannot change a
    # crate's type. It sets its rustc driver up and runs the cargo CARGO names, so a stand-in
    # for that cargo turns its `build` into `rustc --crate-type staticlib`, every other call,
    # its `metadata` among them, passing through. The /opt shim of `cargo bsan` sets CARGO
    # itself, so the real cargo-bsan, the ELF on PATH, is run directly, as the shim runs it.
    out=$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/bsan/$host/debug
    real_cargo=$(type -P cargo)
    real_bsan=
    for c in $(type -ap cargo-bsan); do
      [ "$(head -c4 "$c")" = $'\x7fELF' ] && { real_bsan=$c; break; }
    done
    [ -n "$real_bsan" ] || { echo "rust-staticlib.sh: no cargo-bsan executable on PATH" >&2; exit 1; }
    mkdir -p "$CARGO_TARGET_DIR"
    shim=$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/cargo-rustc-staticlib
    printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/bash' \
      "[ \"\${1:-}\" = build ] || exec '$real_cargo' \"\$@\"" \
      'shift' \
      "exec '$real_cargo' rustc \"\$@\" --crate-type staticlib" >"$shim"
    chmod +x "$shim"
    side=$(realpath -m "$build/../../../..")
    export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="$side/pcre2-bindings/crustify/builds/$variant/install/lib/pkgconfig${PKG_CONFIG_PATH:+:$PKG_CONFIG_PATH}"
    export CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT=$variant
    (cd "$here" && RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=bsan CARGO=$shim "$real_bsan" bsan build "${crate[@]}")
    # The driver bundles BorrowSanitizer's C runtime into the library; the C's own links
    # link it (the variant's CMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS), so that each process holds it once,
    # and a shared library none: its members are removed from the copy written.
    bundled=$(rustc +bsan --print sysroot)/lib/libclang_rt.bsan-x86_64.a
    [ -f "$bundled" ] || { echo "rust-staticlib.sh: no BorrowSanitizer runtime at $bundled" >&2; exit 1; } ;;
  *)
    echo "rust-staticlib.sh: unknown variant: $variant" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

lib=$out/liblibgit2_crustify.a
[ -f "$lib" ] || { echo "rust-staticlib.sh: cargo wrote no $lib" >&2; exit 1; }
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$archive")"
tmp=$archive.tmp.$$
trap 'rm -f "$tmp"' EXIT
cp "$lib" "$tmp"
if [ -n "$bundled" ]; then
  mapfile -t members < <(ar t "$bundled" | sort -u)
  while ar t "$tmp" | grep -qxF -f <(printf '%s\n' "${members[@]}"); do
    ar d "$tmp" "${members[@]}"
  done
  ranlib "$tmp"
fi
mv -f "$tmp" "$archive"
trap - EXIT
echo "rust-staticlib.sh: $archive is the $variant Rust of $here"

# Archive the objects every link unit links into one static archive, so that campaign mode
# links the C statically and reaches the internal functions the shared library hides

# current: <archive> is the archive written, relative to the build dir, as the variant's
# `static` records it in crustify/artifacts/build.json, and each <link unit> names a target
# CMake links: a shared library by its name (libgit2, for libgit2.so) or an executable (git2,
# the CLI). The objects are taken from the build system, the explicit inputs of the edge that
# links each, found through its symlink edges: every TU of the link unit itself and of the
# object libraries it bundles, and nothing else (no test or other target). An object two
# link units both link (the CLI links libgit2's) is archived once, where it first appears.
# Nothing is compiled; the archive is replaced atomically and is deterministic (no
# timestamps), so the same objects give the same bytes.

objects=() names=()
declare -A seen=()
for unit in "$@"; do
  target=$unit.so
7

 "build": "\"${CRUSTIFY_ROOT:?}/crustify/scripts/rust-staticlib.sh\" plain crustify/liblibgit2_crustify.a && cmake --build . && \"${CRUSTIFY_ROOT:?}/crustify/scripts/static-archive.sh\" crustify/libcrustify.a libgit2 git2",
 "static": "crustify/libcrustify.a",
 "rust": "crustify/liblibgit2_crustify.a"
}

---
name: wavefront
description: "Deterministic queries and dependency-ordered plans over the C codebase, the first resort for any question about it: entities, uses, dependencies, pointers, lifecycles, T3 cast tables. Read before querying the C codebase, before planning, decomposing or scheduling, before analysing or binding an item, when packing wrap batches, when reviewing pointer findings or lifecycles, and before changing wavefront itself."
---

# wavefront

Wavefront answers deterministic queries about a C codebase, its entities, their uses and
dependencies, their pointers and lifecycles, and generates dependency-ordered wave plans
over it.

It is the first resort for any question about the C codebase: an entity's definition,
fields or signature, its users, callers and casts, what it depends on, and the pointer
findings and lifecycle roles submitted on it are queried rather than searched for in the
source, so that each answer covers every site the traced build compiles, and every query
of one fact gets one answer. The source is read where wavefront records nothing, to read a
body, and to judge what wavefront records.

Its `README.md` and `--help` are read in full before its first command, and each section
below names the documents under its `docs/` that its stage reads, also in full. How
wavefront scopes, orders and batches, what its configuration, tables and records hold, and
what each query returns are those documents', and are not restated here. Its goals and
non-goals, `docs/goals.md`, are what a change to wavefront is judged against, as
[`evolution`](../../crustify/evolution/SKILL.md) describes.

## Campaign state
## Binding and porting

Binding and porting read `docs/pointer-properties.md`, `docs/type-lifecycle.md`,
`docs/artifacts/findings.md` and `docs/artifacts/t3.md`.

### Analysis

An item's analysis queries the campaign's configuration, and its findings are submitted
to the ownership store. A type-erased parameter or field is looked up in the T3 tables before it
is bound, and the binding names the type a row gives it rather than a raw pointer. The
instances of a type generator share one generic, with per-instance aliases.

### Binding types › Surface

A type's lifecycle primitives are identified as `docs/type-lifecycle.md` describes, and
submitted to the ownership store.

### Binding symbols › Function pointers

A function pointer's record and its users are those of wavefront's function-pointer query,
named as `docs/graph.md`'s Nodes section names it, and the sites of one written inline,
and what reaches them, are as `docs/batching.md`'s Release points section describes.
<!-- TODO: no query lists an inline function pointer's sites yet: they are read from the
table that section names. -->

### Binding symbols › Lifecycle strategies

Each foundational item's lifecycle role is in the ownership store, where planning
submitted it, and is queried for every item of the batch. A role that the item's body
contradicts is corrected in the ownership store, and the correction named in the batch's commit
message.

### Porting types

A ported type's lifecycle primitives are identified as `docs/type-lifecycle.md`

---
name: wavefront
description: "Deterministic queries and dependency-ordered plans over the C codebase, the first resort for any question about it: entities, uses, dependencies, pointers, lifecycles, T3 cast tables. Read before querying the C codebase, before planning, decomposing or scheduling, before analysing or binding an item, when packing wrap batches, when reviewing pointer findings or lifecycles, and before changing wavefront itself."
---

# wavefront

Wavefront answers deterministic queries about a C codebase, its entities, their uses and
dependencies, their pointers and lifecycles, and generates dependency-ordered wave plans
over it.

It is the first resort for any question about the C codebase: an entity's definition,
fields or signature, its users, callers and casts, what it depends on, and the pointer
findings and lifecycle roles submitted on it are queried rather than searched for in the
source, so that each answer covers every site the traced build compiles, and every query
of one fact gets one answer. The source is read where wavefront records nothing, to read a
body, and to judge what wavefront records.

Its `README.md` and `--help` are read in full before its first command, and each section
below names the documents under its `docs/` that its stage reads, also in full. How
wavefront scopes, orders and batches, what its configuration, tables and records hold, and
what each query returns are those documents', and are not restated here. Its goals and
non-goals, `docs/goals.md`, are what a change to wavefront is judged against, as
[`evolution`](../../crustify/evolution/SKILL.md) describes.

## Campaign state
## Binding and porting

Binding and porting read `docs/pointer-properties.md`, `docs/type-lifecycle.md`,
`docs/artifacts/findings.md` and `docs/artifacts/t3.md`.

### Analysis

An item's analysis queries the campaign's configuration, and its findings are submitted
to the ownership store. A type-erased parameter or field is looked up in the T3 tables before it
is bound, and the binding names the type a row gives it rather than a raw pointer. The
instances of a type generator share one generic, with per-instance aliases.

### Binding types › Surface

A type's lifecycle primitives are identified as `docs/type-lifecycle.md` describes, and
submitted to the ownership store.

### Binding symbols › Function pointers

A function pointer's record and its users are those of wavefront's function-pointer query,
named as `docs/graph.md`'s Nodes section names it, and the sites of one written inline,
and what reaches them, are as `docs/batching.md`'s Release points section describes.
<!-- TODO: no query lists an inline function pointer's sites yet: they are read from the
table that section names. -->

### Binding symbols › Lifecycle strategies

Each foundational item's lifecycle role is in the ownership store, where planning
submitted it, and is queried for every item of the batch. A role that the item's body
contradicts is corrected in the ownership store, and the correction named in the batch's commit
message.

### Porting types

A ported type's lifecycle primitives are identified as `docs/type-lifecycle.md`
describes, and submitted to the ownership store.

    extract-ql          Run the T1 (entities) + T2 (edges) .ql batches against

                        write one CSV per query under its codeql/{t1,t2}/. The
                        database is NOT created here — build the project under

                        (filtered, as a name list) or introspect one (--name)

                        external section file sets. `dag` does the graph walks
                        (closure / layer / scc).

# An export whose failure needs an outcome a panic cannot give

Status: `open`.

## Signal

A rule an agent works around: `porting-symbols`' Functions section has a panic caught at an
export's gateway "reported as a failure, or aborts where the function cannot fail", and a
function can fail through a convention that a panic leaves no way to follow.

## Evidence

`wave-186/batch-5/run-1` (`git2/src/cli/opt.c`) exported `cli_opt_parse` and
`cli_opt_parser_next`. Both report their failures through a status and the outcome they write
to the caller's `cli_opt`: the CLI's commands then call `cli_opt_usage_error(cmd, opts,
&invalid_opt)`, which describes that outcome, its spec and argument. A panic in the parse
leaves no outcome to write: a zeroed one with a failing status would make the CLI print
`unknown option: (null)` for an argument that was never unknown. Both gateways abort on a
panic instead, documented on each. `cli_opt_foreach`, whose failure is a bare non-zero
`int` its caller (`common.c`) only tests, reports a panic as `-1`. The rule, read literally,
asks for the failure in all three; the batch departed from it for two.

## Destination

The spec: `porting-symbols`, Functions, the panic sentence.

## Change

Not made; drafted for review:

> A panic is caught at the gateway and reported as a failure where the function's error
> convention can report one from what the gateway holds, its return and the error state
> alone; it aborts where the function cannot fail, or where its convention reports a failure
> through an out-parameter or a buffer the panic left unwritten, which C would read as the
> failure's own: none unwinds into C.

## Validation

None yet: the rerun is `wave-186/batch-5`'s gateways under the changed rule, which they
already follow.

# 1. The CLI's clones. <expect> is ok or fail.
clone() {
  local name=$1 url=$2 expect=$3 dir=$out/clones/$1
  mkdir -p "$out/clones"
  (cd "$out/clones" && timeout 600 "$d/git2" clone "$url" "$dir" >"$dir.out" 2>"$dir.err" </dev/null)
  local rc=$?
  local line="clone $name rc=$rc"
  if [ $rc -eq 0 ] && [ -d "$dir/.git" ]; then
    local refs head tree fsck
    refs=$(git -C "$dir" for-each-ref --format='%(objectname) %(refname)' | sha256sum | cut -c1-16)
    head=$(git -C "$dir" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null)
    tree=$(git -C "$dir" status --porcelain --untracked-files=all | sha256sum | cut -c1-16)
    git -C "$dir" fsck --connectivity-only --no-progress >"$dir.fsck" 2>&1 && fsck=ok || fsck=failed
    line+=" refs=$refs head=$head status=$tree fsck=$fsck"
  else
    line+=" error=\"$(grep -v '^\s*$' "$dir.err" | grep -vE 'Sanitizer|^ +#|^SUMMARY|^==' | tail -1)\""
